title: On Least Squares Approximations for Shapley Values and Applications to Interpretable Machine Learning
content: The Shapley value stands as the predominant point-valued solution concept in cooperative game theory and has recently become a foundational method in interpretable machine learning. In that domain, a prevailing strategy to circumvent the computational intractability of exact Shapley values is to approximate them by reframing their computation as a weighted least squares optimization problem. We investigate an algorithmic framework by Benati et al. (2019), discuss its feasibility for feature attribution and explore a set of methodological and theoretical refinements, including an approach for sample reuse across strata and a relation to Unbiased KernelSHAP. We conclude with an empirical evaluation of the presented algorithms, assessing their performance on several cooperative games including practical problems from interpretable machine learning.
